context: Without the true skeleton, a “local algorithm” (such as ours) can be tricked into some “local optima” and it is hard to argue why the output would obtain “global guarantees” with respect to the parent sets of Eq. (1). Another interesting open question is whether one can extend the hardness result to arbitrary d ≥ 1, or design more efficient learning algorithms for d-polytrees. In particular, we are unaware of any obstruction a lower bound for |Σ| > 2 and d > 2. While we do not know an optimal construction, the following construction (emulating Appendix A.2 of Canonne et al. (2020)) yields n2d n Ω( (d+1)ε 2 ), showing that the exponential dependence on d is unavoidable. Consider d+1 stars with binary alphabets, where each star center has d incoming parents. Each parental node is set to be an independent uniform coin flip over the binary alphabet and so it takes Ω(2d /ε2 ) to learn each star to accuracy ε. As KL is additive, one would require any constant fraction of the stars to incur less n2d than ε(d+1) n error. To do so, one would need Ω( (d+1)ε2 ) samples.
